prompt: A public browser lets users chat. The client suggests hiding the download button until Google sign-in. Is that sufficient to protect Terraform generation and downloads? Explain the trust boundaries and what must be implemented and tested. Do not draw a proposal, request tools, ask a question or claim tests ran. Keep the answer under 180 words.

response.message:
We want public chat with protected Terraform generation and downloads; hiding the button is insufficient because anyone can call the underlying endpoints directly.

The browser and chat/model output are untrusted; Google establishes identity, while our backend must decide permission. Implement server-verified Google sign-in, checking signature, issuer, audience and expiry, with secure sessions and CSRF protection where cookies authenticate requests. Bind anonymous conversations to the authenticated owner through a server-controlled handoff.

Enforce authorization on every generation request, job-status lookup and download, checking project, tenant and artifact ownership. Workers need scoped service identities; artifact storage must be private, with authorized streaming or short-lived download links. Keep cloud credentials server-side, validate generator inputs, isolate execution, and add quotas and audit logs. Sign-in must never imply deployment permission.

Test direct endpoint calls with no login, forged/expired credentials, another user’s project/job/artifact IDs, logout/session expiry, CSRF, anonymous-chat takeover, public storage access, leaked/expired links and concurrent quota bypasses, plus successful authorized flows. These controls require implementation and verification; no tests have run here.
